title.value: Implications of Topological Imbalance for Representation Learning on Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the central theme of the paper, which is to understand the effect of structural imbalances within Knowledge Graphs, specifically in the context of representation learning and its implications for drug discovery.
title.quote: Implications of Topological Imbalance for Representation Learning on Biomedical Knowledge Graphs

extractions.description: The paper investigates how topological imbalances in biomedical Knowledge Graphs (KGs) influence representation learning, particularly in drug discovery applications. It highlights that entities with high connectivity tend to be ranked higher in predictive tasks, which can overshadow biologically meaningful predictions. The study emphasizes the need for careful data modeling and interpretation when constructing and using KGs for predictive tasks.

primary_category.justification: The paper is primarily concerned with the methodological aspect of learning from Knowledge Graphs in biomedical applications, specifically drug discovery. It does not directly address any eco-responsible category, such as climate change or pollution.
primary_category.quote: Our results highlight the importance of data modeling choices, and emphasizes the need for practitioners to be mindful of these issues when interpreting model outputs and during KG composition.

secondary_categories.justification: The study does not explore applications or implications in any secondary eco-responsible domains as defined by the provided categories. Its focus remains strictly within biomedical data modeling and representation learning.
secondary_categories.quote: In this study, we aim to fill in this gap by providing a comprehensive analysis of how structural imbalance in the underlying data in a KG affects the scores for predicted relationships.

primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper does not relate to eco-responsible AI categories, it similarly does not fit into any eco-responsible sub-categories. Its insights are relevant to AI representation learning in the biomedical domain.
primary_sub_category.quote: One common application is to produce ranked lists of genes for a given disease, where the rank is based on the perceived likelihood of association between the gene and the disease.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Secondary assessments within eco-responsible sub-categories are not applicable as the paper focuses exclusively on biomedical Knowledge Graphs and representation learning, without addressing any eco-responsible AI topics.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We demonstrate that the KGE methods tend to overrate the highly-connected entities, and that this result is reproducible in different datasets (i.e. graphs), for different embedding models, across different diseases and different predictive tasks.

applications.value: Drug target prediction using Knowledge Graphs
applications.justification: The paper focuses on using KG embedding methods for predicting associations between genes and diseases, which is a foundational task in drug discovery.
applications.quote: For example, performing drug target identification has been addressed as link prediction between gene and disease entities using the ComplEx model [47] on a drug discovery graph [32].

new_primary_category.justification: The content primarily revolves around the challenges and implications of using Knowledge Graphs and embedding methods within the domain of biomedical data, suggesting a new category specific to this field.
new_primary_category.quote: Adoption of recently developed methods from machine learning has given rise to creation of drug-discovery knowledge graphs (KG) that utilize the interconnected nature of the domain.

new_primary_sub_category.value: Topological Imbalance in Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
new_primary_sub_category.justification: This sub-category is suggested due to the paper's focus on the uneven representation of entities in Knowledge Graphs influencing predictive tasks in drug discovery.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our results highlight the importance of data modeling choices, and emphasizes the need for practitioners to be mindful of these issues when interpreting model outputs and during KG composition.
